transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Velasquez (Redwood SE), Lena Korsakov (GlobalTranslate Head of ML), Diego Morales (Platform), Alyssa Park (PM), Ravi Singh (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to validate model fit for multilingual translation+extraction workflows across EU and APAC, discuss success criteria (latency, quality, cost), workload sizing, shortlist of open models for pilot, and timeline for a 3-month pilot. Customer emphasized strict data residency and audit logs.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and KPIs (BLEU/ChrF alternatives, latency p95, end-to-end SLA)
- Workload sizing: QPS, token distribution, peak vs steady
- Benchmark plan and metrics (quality + perf)
- Open-model shortlist and tradeoffs (size, quantization, multilingual coverage)
- Deployment choices (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)
- Compliance needs (KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros real quick, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account. Omar is our solutions engineer. Lena?
[00:10] Lena (GlobalTranslate): Hi, Lena here, head of ML at GlobalTranslate. We're looking to run a proof-of-concept for our multilingual pipeline.
[00:18] Diego: Diego, infra. we'll be the ones running the benchmark on our side and coordinating with platform ops.
[00:22] Omar (Redwood SE): Awesome, thanks. high-level goal — validate open models for our translate+entity extraction pipeline, and get sizing for dedicated capacity if needed.
[00:30] Alyssa (PM): Quick note from product: target is 20ms token latency p95 ideally for short-form translation, and overall throughput to support 150 rps peak for our real-time API.
[00:40] Ravi (Compliance): And for us, must prove data never leaves EU for EU dataset; we need audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:47] Maya: Understood. okay let's walk success criteria first, then sizing, then models and bench.
[00:53] Lena: For quality, we use a combined metric — prefer chrF+ semantic similarity (embedding-based) over raw BLEU since we care about downstream NER performance. Our pass threshold is: chrF >= 0.55 on our dev slice and NER F1 drop <= 2% compared to current in-house baseline.
[01:15] Omar: Got it — so bench metrics will include chrF, embedding-sim, and NER F1, plus latency p50/p95 and token cost. We'll instrument both model output and run an eval pipeline.
[01:30] Diego: Regarding QPS, our baseline steady is 20 rps, peak 150 rps; average input length is about 120 tokens per request, with 95th percentile at 480 tokens. That greatly changes batching behavior and GPU memory needs.
[01:48] Maya: Great detail. are you expecting mostly short requests for UI (low latency) or batch jobs as well?
[01:53] Alyssa: Mix of both — UI should feel instant, so low-latency route; also nightly bulk translation where throughput matters.
[02:03] Lena: Also note, we have 12 target languages initially: EN, FR, DE, ES, PT, NL, RU, PL, JA, KO, ZH, AR. Multilingual coverage is a key filter.
[02:15] Omar: For model shortlist, we proposed these open models: 1) MosaicMTranslate-13B (quantized 4-bit), 2) Polyglot-7B-mt (multilingual optimized), 3) OmniLLaMA-30B-llm (float16), and 4) Electra-ish-XL (lightweight distilled). We'll rank by quality vs cost tradeoffs.
[02:38] Lena: Names might be slightly off — but yes, that style. Can you walk us through the expected quality differences?
[02:45] Omar: Sure — OmniLLaMA-30B gives best out-of-the-box quality on Asian languages and rare scripts, but needs more memory and yields higher token cost. MosaicMTranslate-13B with 4-bit quant can hit pretty competitive chrF for Romance languages and is cheaper; Polyglot-7B optimized for many-to-many translation might give balanced quality at low cost; Electra-ish-XL is for latency-constrained cases but may lose 3-5% on NER downstream.
[03:12] Maya: Important note — we can run mixed routing: host small latency-critical models on Dedicated low-latency nodes and route bulk requests to cheaper quantized variants to save cost.
[03:24] Diego: For Dedicated we need throughput numbers — how many tokens/sec per GPU for each model variant? can you provide ballpark?
[03:30] Omar: Rough ballpark on A100-ish: OmniLLaMA-30B ~ 18-22 tok/s per GPU at 1-thread sampling for generation with kv cache warm; MosaicMTranslate-13B 45-60 tok/s with 4-bit kernels; Polyglot-7B ~ 120-160 tok/s quant; Electra-ish-XL ~ 250+ tok/s. These are very workload dependent — we will bench with your token length distribution.
[03:58] Ravi: For compliance, do you support customer-managed KMS and per-request audit logs? and can you store logs in our S3 within EU?
[04:07] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer KMS and configurable audit logs; we can also push audit events to your S3 in region or integrate with your SIEM. We'll include the security whitepaper.
[04:17] Alyssa: Timeline — we're aiming to start pilot in mid-Oct and run for ~8 weeks of evaluation, then a 3-month pilot for production readiness. Is that feasible?
[04:25] Omar: Feasible. For benchmarking we'll propose a 2-week sprint: week 1 run initial bench across models on synthetic slices, week 2 run real-data slices and NLU regressions. After that we'll review quality and cost and select pilot model(s).
[04:40] Lena: How do you handle multilang fine-tuning vs prompting? we prefer no full fine-tune for now; prefer prompt + small instruction tuning or LoRA for a later phase.
[04:50] Omar: That's fine. For POC we'll do zero-shot / few-shot and small LoRA experiments only if needed. That keeps the compute manageable.
[04:58] Diego: For the benchmark harness, we need a reproducible docker / k8s recipe. can you provide sample configs and resource reqs?
[05:06] Omar: Yes, we'll provide a harness plus a sample dockerfile. we'll include options for running on Dedicated GPUs and a hosted pathway we can instrument.
[05:14] Maya: Let's talk detailed success criteria and pass/fail gates. Lena?
[05:18] Lena: Primary gate is quality: chrF >= 0.55 and NER F1 drop <= 2%. Secondary gate is p95 latency <= 250ms for UI routing on the latency model, and cost per 1M tokens <= $X (we'll put a ballpark during follow-up). Also must meet residency: EU data not leaving EU during bench or pilot.
[05:40] Maya: We'll include those gates in the bench template. Omar will instrument p50/p95 latency, cold vs warm start, and token-level cost.
[05:48] Ravi: On audit logs, we need proof that API calls and outputs are logged with non-reversible IDs and can be exported monthly. is that straightforward?
[05:56] Maya: Yes, we support export of audit logs; we will map the fields you'll need. we'll attach the schema.
[06:02] Alyssa: Any known weaknesses in the open models for Arabic/Hebrew or right-to-left?
[06:08] Omar: Some models have weaker support for morphological-rich languages, Arabic included. OmniLLaMA-30B tends to be better there; Polyglot-7B sometimes drops accuracy on low-resource languages. We'll run targeted slices for those languages.
[06:21] Diego: For resource planning — if we want to support 150 rps peak with typical token lengths, what's the recommended cluster?
[06:28] Omar: Rough estimate: if Polyglot-7B gives 140 tok/s per GPU, with average 120 tokens/request, that's ~1.16 requests/sec per GPU — so you'd need many GPUs for 150 rps. But batching and multi-request pipelining changes that. For latency-critical path you'd probably run smaller models ded-icated per region with autoscale for bursts; for bulk work you can centralize. We'll do detailed sizing after the bench run.
[06:52] Lena: That sounds like a lot, can you show cost tradeoffs? we want a table: model, cost per 1M tokens hosted, dedicated monthly estimate, expected quality.
[07:01] Maya: We'll produce that table as part of the follow-up.
[07:05] Alyssa: Another ask — can we run the bench on-prem for a subset? regulatory says some EU customers require physical isolation.
[07:13] Omar: We can support Private on-prem deployments. Depending on the hardware you provide, we can ship an appliance or give install guidance. For POC we typically start on Hosted or Redwood Dedicated in an EU region to speed up time-to-result, then extend to on-prem if needed.
[07:29] Ravi: We'll need SOC2 and ISO docs and an INR compliance note.
[07:34] Maya: We'll attach SOC2 bridge letter and ISO docs.
[07:37] Diego: About the benchmark dataset — we'll give you a 10k-sentence anonymized dev set across languages and an additional 50k synthetic burst set for throughput. Is that enough?
[07:46] Lena: Yes, that should be fine. we'll also provide NER labels for the dev slices.
[07:51] Omar: Perfect. For the bench harness we'll compute chrF and an embedding sim score using your embed model. Note: embedding models differ across vendors; we'll use a fixed embed baseline to be consistent.
[08:03] Alyssa: Ok, walk through the POC milestones and timeline for October/November.
[08:08] Maya: Proposed milestones:
- Oct 2: Deliver model shortlist + bench template + security docs
- Oct 6: Customer provides dataset slices and confirms residency
- Oct 8-10: Initial synthetic perf runs (hosted/dedicated)
- Oct 13-17: Real-data bench runs and NER regression tests
- Oct 20: Review results and pick pilot model
- Nov 1: Start 3-month pilot (if go)
[08:33] Lena: That aligns with our internal timeline. good.
[08:36] Ravi: On data retention — can we set short TTL for logs and also a separate archived copy retained longer?
[08:43] Maya: Yes, configurable retention windows are possible and we can push archives to your archive bucket.
[08:48] Diego: technical deep dive question — how do you handle KV cache across multilingual contexts and prompt-switching? any impact on memory?
[08:56] Omar: KV cache size scales with sequence length and model size. for frequent context-switching we'll recommend smaller per-request sequences or warmed shards. also continuous batching and prefix caching can reduce repeated compute for common prefixes. We'll capture these as knobs in the bench.
[09:12] Lena: For model variants — what's the upgrade path if we later want to do LoRA tuning or bespoke domain adapt?
[09:18] Omar: After POC, if LoRA helps, we can coordinate a small 10-20k step LoRA fine-tune in your region. Redwood Dedicated supports storing tuned weights and serving them alongside base model versions.
[09:29] Alyssa: Any extra telemetry we should expect from Redwood Console for the pilot?
[09:33] Maya: Console gives token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, model-specific dashboards, and failure traces. We'll enable an initial retention window and expand if needed.
[09:43] Diego: About cost, can Redwood provide a bounded estimate for the Dedicated cluster for pilot? we need a procurement number.
[09:50] Maya: We'll provide a conservative estimate — e.g., two racks equivalent for EU region for 3 months, with commit tiers and an option to burst hosted. We'll include line items in the follow-up.
[09:58] Ravi: One more compliance ask — can we demonstrate encryption-in-transit + at-rest and HSM-backed keys?
[10:04] Omar: Yes, we support HSM-backed KMS for Private deployments and envelope encryption for Hosted. We'll attach the architecture note.
[10:12] Alyssa: Back to model tradeoffs: which model would you recommend we initially benchmark across all languages?
[10:18] Omar: Recommend Polyglot-7B and MosaicMTranslate-13B as a baseline (cost/latency balance), and OmniLLaMA-30B for a high-quality control. Electra-ish-XL only if latency wins over quality. That gives you 3 axis coverage.
[10:34] Lena: Fine. and we'll add Arabic and Chinese as high-priority test slices.
[10:38] Maya: Great. we'll include the specific model hashes/versions in the follow-up.
[10:43] Diego: Are there any known tokenization differences we should normalize?
[10:47] Omar: Yes, tokenizers differ; part of the bench is ensuring you run a consistent tokenizer (we can use a universal normalization pre-step). We'll provide scripts.
[10:56] Alyssa: Questions from procurement — SLA for Dedicated pilot?
[11:00] Maya: We can offer an SLA with uptime and latency targets for Dedicated pilots. Formal terms will be in the pilot contract.
[11:07] Ravi: Anything else from security?
[11:09] Ravi: No, that's covered. we'll review the docs once they arrive.
[11:12] Maya: Okay quick recap of next steps — Maya will send shortlist + bench template + SOC2/ISO docs by Oct 2. Omar will push benchmark harness and example dockerfile. Lena will share dataset slices by Oct 6. Tentative 2-week bench starting Oct 8.
[11:29] Lena: Sounds good to me.
[11:31] Diego: yep.
[11:32] Alyssa: thanks all.
[11:35] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[11:36] (call ends)
